economics.assumptions-describe.0012.all: Workers also value non-wage benefits, e.g. job satisfaction, location/shorter commute, flexible hours, so a lower-paid job may give greater total reward.

economics.assumptions-explain.0016.all: Rewards include non-financial benefits; staying close to home saves travel time and cost and gives more leisure/family time; so Marisol's total reward may be greater than the higher wage at Riverstone Apparel.

economics.bop-analyse-1.0006.all: High spending on imported electronics/cars raises outflows; falling manufactured exports cut inflows (uncompetitive: high costs, strong currency, low productivity); persistent 5 years at 6.8% GDP suggests structural causes.

economics.bop-analyse-2.0006.all: Manufactured export revenue raises AD, GDP, jobs; surplus can build reserves/invest abroad; appreciation makes imports cheaper, lowering inflation and raising living standards.

economics.bop-assess-1.0002.all: Consequences: pressure on currency, lost jobs in manufacturing, lower AD, borrowing/selling assets to finance. Evaluation: consumers gain imported goods, may be financed by FDI, capital imports may raise growth, depreciation may self-correct; 7 years at 6.8% is serious.

economics.bop-assess-2.0002.all: Good: jobs, growth, reserves. Not always: reliance on gas risky, appreciation hurts other exporters, may reflect low domestic consumption, trade retaliation. Judgement.

economics.bop-define1.0001.all: A record of all financial transactions between a country and the rest of the world.

economics.bop-define2.0001.all: A record of all financial transactions (1) between one country and the rest of the world (1).

economics.bop-describe.0015.all: It may be due to imports of capital goods that raise future productive capacity / exports; or small and short-term, financed by FDI inflows.

economics.bop-explain.0015.all: Tourist spending is an export of services; money flows into Istrova; recorded as a credit (I$10bn) in trade in services on the current account, improving the balance.

economics.bop-mcq-def.0004.all: When the value of money flowing in on the current account is greater than the money flowing out

economics.bop-state.0008.all: Trade in goods (or services, primary income, secondary income).

economics.competition-analyse-1.0001.all: Interdependence: a price cut would be matched, causing price war and lower profits; so firms compete through advertising/branding to build loyalty and make demand less price elastic; 75% share means large budgets; raises barriers to entry.

economics.competition-analyse-2.0005.all: Price maker so high prices; no alternative supplier for a necessity (inelastic demand); no incentive to improve poor service; large profits at consumers' expense; less innovation/choice.

economics.competition-analyse-3.0002.all: Lower prices raise real incomes; more choice and convenience (next-day delivery); shops must improve service/quality; innovation.

economics.competition-assess-1.0003.all: Benefits: scale economies, innovation funded by profits, quality from non-price competition. Costs: similar prices suggest collusion, higher prices, advertising costs passed on, limited choice. Judgement.

economics.competition-assess-2.0005.all: For: lower fares, better service, efficiency. Against: natural monopoly, duplication of track, economies of scale, investment from profits; regulation alternative. Judgement.

economics.competition-assess-3.0006.all: Negative: lower sales, profits, closures (14%), job losses. Positive: pressure to cut costs, innovate, go online, differentiate. Judgement depends on adaptability.

economics.competition-define1.0005.all: A firm that can set the price of its product (has market power).

economics.competition-define2.0007.all: When firms agree with each other (1) to fix prices/output or share markets, reducing competition (1).

economics.competition-describe.0010.all: Advertising/branding: firms promote their product to build brand loyalty, so demand rises and becomes less price elastic.

economics.competition-evaluate-1.0003.all: Plan: benefits (scale economies, innovation, quality) vs costs (similar prices suggest collusion, high prices, advertising costs, barriers); 81% share; judgement depends on regulation.

economics.competition-evaluate-2.0004.all: Plan: competition lowers prices and improves service; but water is a natural monopoly, duplication wasteful, safety; regulation alternative; judgement.

economics.competition-evaluate-3.0001.all: Plan: lost sales, closures 11%, job losses; but incentive to innovate, cut costs, go online, specialise; judgement on time frame and type of firm.

economics.bop-analyse-1.0006.problem: Question asks for causes but indicative content includes consequences (financing by borrowing/selling assets, job losses in export industries).
economics.bop-analyse-1.0006.fix: Replace last two bullets with causes, e.g. high incomes/consumer spending, strong currency, low productivity, high inflation relative to trading partners.

economics.competition-analyse-2.0005.problem: Incoherent context: a firm called Northgate Textiles is the only supplier of electricity.
economics.competition-analyse-2.0005.fix: Rename the firm to fit the industry, e.g. Northgate Power.

economics.competition-assess-2.0005.problem: Incoherent context: Lumo Energy is the only supplier of rail travel.
economics.competition-assess-2.0005.fix: Rename the firm to fit the industry, e.g. Lumo Rail.

economics.competition-assess-3.0006.problem: Question asks impact on firms, but indicative content is about consumers (lower prices, convenience, choice, consumers unable to shop online).
economics.competition-assess-3.0006.fix: Use firm-focused content: falling sales/profits, 14% closures, need to cut costs, innovate, go online or differentiate; efficient firms survive; online retailer gains market share/scale.

economics.competition-evaluate-2.0004.problem: Incoherent context: Tamarind Retail is the only supplier of water.
economics.competition-evaluate-2.0004.fix: Rename the firm to fit the industry, e.g. Tamarind Water.

economics.competition-evaluate-3.0001.problem: Question asks impact on firms, but indicative content is about consumers (lower prices, convenience, choice, consumers unable to shop online).
economics.competition-evaluate-3.0001.fix: Use firm-focused content: falling sales/profits, 11% closures, need to cut costs, innovate, go online or differentiate; online retailer gains; judgement on adaptability/time frame.
